name: sotn-cmd
description: Runs an allowlisted set of SOTN build, diff, permuter, git and queue actions in WSL.
long_description:
Gives Claude a hard-allowlisted set of repo actions. There is NO general shell.

Every argument is validated (version enum, strict regexes for symbols and overlays, in-repo path checks), commands run as an argv list rather than through a shell, and output is truncated. Scoped filesystem actions let Claude read and edit the repo when the folder is not connected directly.

Ships with dry-run ENABLED: every tool returns the exact command it would run without executing it. Turn dry-run off only after reviewing what it produces.

THIS BUNDLE IS A LAUNCHER AND CONTAINS ONLY THIS MANIFEST. The MCPB spec allows that: a manifest.json is the only required file. mcp_config cd's into the repo and runs automation/mcp from there, so the connector always executes the live source and an edit takes effect on the next Claude Desktop restart, with no repack and no reinstall.

It used to also carry server/commands_client.py and server/sotn_cmd_mcp.py. Those were snapshots taken when the bundle was first built and were never executed again; by 2026-08-09 the client copy had drifted to 18808 bytes against the live 66551 and still contained an _inrepo path-containment bug that an external audit found and that was fixed in the live copy the same day. A stale duplicate of security-relevant code is worse than no copy: it is what a reader or an auditor lands on, and every fix has to be remembered twice. Deleted, so there is one authoritative copy of each tool.

entry_point names the file the launcher runs, which lives in the repo rather than in this archive. Nothing reads it at runtime; mcp_config is what executes. Confirmed by running `mcpb validate`: the manifest is checked against the schema only, never against the archive's contents.

THIS BUNDLE IS NOT THE SERVER, AND IT IS NOT REQUIRED. The server is automation/mcp/sotn_cmd_mcp.py, a plain stdio MCP server with no client detection and no vendor SDK. Any MCP client can launch it directly: OpenAI Codex CLI, Claude Code, Continue, Cline, or anything else that can spawn a process. Ready-made registrations live in automation/mcp/clients/ (a Codex TOML, a generic native JSON, and a Windows-plus-WSL JSON), and docs/CONNECTORS.md explains the choice.

The `compatibility` block below is narrow ON PURPOSE and describes THIS BUNDLE, not the server. MCPB is a Claude Desktop packaging format and its ${user_config} substitution is a Claude Desktop feature, so a bundle is only meaningful to that client; and this particular mcp_config shells through wsl.exe, which is a Windows host reaching a Linux toolchain. Neither limit applies to the Python server. Reading `platforms: [win32]` as 'the harness is Windows-only' would be exactly the wrong conclusion.

THE `tools` ARRAY BELOW IS A THIRD SURFACE AND IT DRIFTS. commands_client.REGISTRY is the shell allowlist, the @mcp.tool() decorators in sotn_cmd_mcp.py are what is actually callable, and this array is what a reader of the bundle sees. Until 2026-08-17 it listed 21 tools while the connector exposed 72, so anyone reading the bundle to learn the surface was reading a months-old subset. automation/test_connector_surfaces.py now asserts this array equals the callable set exactly and names any tool that is missing, so adding a tool without listing it here fails a test instead of quietly misinforming. `list_allowed` remains the live answer.

tools.name: list_allowed
tools.description: Show the allowlist, the callable tool surface, and the dry-run state. Call this first.

tools.name: make_build
tools.description: make build VERSION=<v>. Exclusive: takes the BuildLock.

tools.name: make_extract
tools.description: make extract VERSION=<v>. Needs the disc image in disks/.

tools.name: make_expected
tools.description: make expected VERSION=<v>. Snapshot the current build as the reference.

tools.name: make_force_symbols
tools.description: Extract symbols from a good build

tools.name: verify_build
tools.description: Hash every overlay against config/check.<v>.sha. THE ORACLE.

tools.name: asm_diff
tools.description: Run asm-differ for one function. Needs the overlay name, not just the symbol.

tools.name: permuter
tools.description: Run decomp-permuter on an in-repo work dir. debug=True scores the base only.

tools.name: permuter_import
tools.description: Prepare a permuter work dir from a seed

tools.name: run_analysis
tools.description: Run one read-only analysis script from ANALYSIS_SCRIPTS

tools.name: opencode_preflight
tools.description: Fail a doomed fleet fast, before workers start

tools.name: fleet_start
tools.description: Start N model workers. backend defaults to zen.

tools.name: fleet_status
tools.description: Fleet state plus log tails. Read the tails: a stuck worker looks alive.

tools.name: fleet_stop
tools.description: Stop the fleet, release claims, replay crash journals. ALWAYS run this.

tools.name: job_start
tools.description: Start a long action asynchronously and return a job id

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Poll a job. elapsed_s includes queue wait, so it is not a runtime.

tools.name: job_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a job and write its exit sentinel

tools.name: queue_init
tools.description: Seed the queue from a seed file

tools.name: queue_list
tools.description: List queue records, optionally by status

tools.name: queue_report
tools.description: Set a record's status/score/notes. proof is REQUIRED for matched.

tools.name: queue_annotate
tools.description: Attach twin candidates to records. Writes only the twin field.

tools.name: queue_prune
tools.description: Remove records that are not real functions

tools.name: queue_snapshot
tools.description: Copy the live queue into the repo so a git checkpoint can hold it. Call before any checkpoint.

tools.name: queue_restore
tools.description: Replace the live queue with a snapshot. Requires confirm; snapshots what it replaces first.

tools.name: mcpb_validate
tools.description: Validate a bundle manifest against the schema

tools.name: mcpb_pack
tools.description: Pack a bundle directory into an .mcpb

tools.name: git_state
tools.description: Branch, HEAD, upstream and dirty summary in one call

tools.name: git_submodule_state
tools.description: Read porcelain-v2 status inside one declared submodule

tools.name: git_submodule_diff
tools.description: Read a working-tree, staged, or stat diff inside one declared submodule

tools.name: git_show_file
tools.description: Show a file at a revision

tools.name: git_add
tools.description: Stage ONE explicit path. Prefer this over git_add_all.

tools.name: git_add_all
tools.description: git add -A. The harness writes constantly; this sweeps its output into your commit.

tools.name: git_checkout_path
tools.description: Adopt one path from a revision, e.g. an upstream header

tools.name: git_mv
tools.description: Rename a tracked file. Refuses when a splat segment still names the old stem.

tools.name: git_rm
tools.description: Delete a tracked file. Same splat guard.

tools.name: git_restore
tools.description: Restore a path. Refuses on orphaned src/ work.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write an in-repo text file (respects dry-run)

tools.name: search_repo
tools.description: Search the repo (ripgrep/grep, argv-safe). Pass regex=True for alternation.

repo_path.title: Repository path (as WSL sees it)
repo_path.description: Absolute WSL path to the sotn-decomp repo. A Windows folder C:\Users\you\Documents\SOTN-Decomp is /mnt/c/Users/you/Documents/SOTN-Decomp in WSL.

wsl_distro.title: WSL distribution
wsl_distro.description: Which WSL distro to run in. Must be the one with the build toolchain, not docker-desktop.

dry_run.title: Dry run (1 = preview only, 0 = actually execute)
dry_run.description: Leave at 1 until you have reviewed the commands it produces. At 1 every tool returns the argv it would run and changes nothing.
